title: RBC Training Ground 2017 Vancouver winner: Meet Avalon Wasteneys
description: The 19-year-old former cross-country skier from Victoria B.C. decided to try out at the RBC Training Ground event at the last minute and won. CBC Sports looks at what Avalon has been up to since winning the regional final and talks to the athlete about what she sees in her future.  http://cbcsports.ca/trainingground  Subscribe to CBC Sports: http://bit.ly/CBCSportsSub  CONNECT WITH CBC SPORTS ON SOCIAL Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/CBCSports Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/cbc.sports  Twitter: https://twitter.com/cbcsports  Google+: http://bit.ly/CBCSportsGooglePlus   Read CBC Sports Online: http://bit.ly/CBCSportsWebsite   [Video Title] https://www.youtube.com/user/CBCSports

asr.full_text: This class ... and I'm Givin' it ... Givin' it … Nearly a hundred amazing young athletes pushed to the limit. You can't help but be in awe of all of them. Keep going! Keep going! Keep going! Keep going! On the girl's side I think we've come to the conclusion that there was one athlete that really stood out head and shoulders above the rest. Karen and myself, our great honor to call up Avalon Wesmeath from Canberra River, CO! It s a pleasure to play against you and your team! Well done! Can I say your name? Avalon Westmeath from Canberra, CO! Avalon Westmeath from Canberra, CO! This 19 year old's life is about to change. We ve come to Victoria to check in on Avalon. with their goal at the time. We've come to Victoria to check in on Avalon. Everyone at the University Victoria's Rowing Team knows she's a special athlete, but her last minute decision to compete in RBC Training Ground made her believe it too. I literally decided the night before to go to qualifiers and I was like OK sure, I'll just go for fun and And then I ended up winning so I was kind of shocked, I was like oh, really? Me? Maybe the reason she was so surprised is because she started rowing less than two years ago. You see, Avalon grew up cross-country skiing and made it to the Junior National Level, but she was raised in a family of rowers. My mom was a rower. She was in Olympic team for 1984-1988. My aunt was a rower. My dad was a rower, both my siblings like is just in the family I guess. For years, Avalon resisted her mom's please to follow in her footsteps. And I'd always just laugh like no mom like I will not do that, skiing is the perfect sport for me but once I made that decision by myself I just immediately got excited and I haven't looked back. Since winning RBC Training Ground Avalon is looking to the future. She's working with Rowan Canada, on developing a road map for herself. What I feel like has happened for Avalon in the last couple of months is that she've started to really put some detail to that pathway. I think that's the coolest thing about this event and about this project. Through RBC Training Ground, Avalon now has access to specialized training and coaching as well as financial support to become a full time athlete this summer. It's also given her the belief that she can be an Olympian one day. It did make me, you know, like, okay, I can do this. Other people think I can do this. So, I'm more dedicated I fee like now, you know okay I can't do this other people think I can do this so I I more dedicated I feel like now to push myself it's been a dream one day to come to the Olympics given all the feedback I got from other people at coaches and family members I definitely feel like I'm on the right path and I've personally been enjoying it a lot.
